title: Data, streaming & background work
summary: The Nimbus API gets **Nimbus Notes**: notes stored with **SQLModel**, documents uploaded as text or PDF and downloaded as Markdown, chat answers about your notes **streamed** as Server-Sent Events or over a **WebSocket**, and summaries written by the model **after** the response, as a background task. Measured on a real server: what the user waits for.
learn: **SQLModel**: tables that are also API models, a session per request, CRUD with pagination, 409 for duplicates
**Files and forms**: UploadFile, type and size limits, text from PDFs, downloads
**Streaming**: Server-Sent Events token by token, JSON Lines, time to first event
**WebSockets**: authenticate before accepting, a conversation per connection
**Background tasks**: work after the response, and their limits
flow:
POST /notes ──→ save (SQLModel) ──→ 201 at once ──→ background: summarise with the model
POST /notes/upload (PDF, text) ──→ notes
POST /chat/stream ──→ event: sources ──→ event: token … ──→ event: done
WS /chat/ws?token=… ──→ question ⇄ streamed answer, history per connection

path.title: Production path: Nimbus Notes, part 1
path.summary: Notes live in the database with one model per direction; uploads become notes; chat streams sources and tokens; summaries are written in the background so saving never waits for the model.

steps.title: Data
steps.explain: Note is a table with a unique (owner, title); NoteCreate, NoteUpdate and NotePublic are what clients send and see. A session per request; IntegrityError becomes 409.
production: SQLite for the course; the same models run on Postgres with a different api_database_url.

steps.title: Files
steps.explain: upload() checks the type (415) and reads at most limit + 1 bytes (413); PDFs are read in memory with PyMuPDF; download() sends Markdown with Content-Disposition.
production: Scan uploads before indexing them in production (RAG track: quarantine).

steps.title: Stream
steps.explain: POST /chat/stream sends the sources first, then tokens, then done; the WebSocket keeps a conversation per connection and checks the token before accepting.
production: Proxies must not buffer text/event-stream (nginx: proxy_buffering off).

steps.title: Evaluate
steps.explain:
Three chat questions as JSON and as SSE, and three notes saved with the summary inline and in the background, on a real uvicorn server.

| | first words on screen (p50) | whole answer (p50) | saving a note (p50) |
|---|---|---|---|
| JSON answer, summary written inline | 2.44 s | 2.44 s | 2.92 s |
| **SSE answer, summary in the background** | **1.89 s** | **2.20 s** | **0.007 s** |

On short answers the stream's head start is modest (the model's own first-token time is about 1.6 s), but the sources event arrives at once, and longer answers gain more. Saving a note no longer waits for the model at all: the summary appears a few seconds later, and a failed summary is logged instead of failing the save. Measured on a real uvicorn server, after the background summaries had finished, so no request queued behind another in the rate limiter.
production: Background tasks are lost on restart: the Production track moves must-not-be-lost work to a queue.
